scope: Author-reviewed diagrams tied to the revised manuscript and versioned evidence. Not independent certification or production validation.

figures.title: From anomaly to investigation
figures.subtitle: Malicious Activity as a Statistical Signal

panels.label: Scope
panels.text: 14 operational families + multi-event correlation. These are overlapping analytical views.

panels.label: Evidence boundary
panels.text: Incident reports, functional tests and synthetic statistics answer different questions.

figures.boundary: An anomaly is a lead, not an intrusion verdict or actor attribution.
figures.caption: A detection-engineering workflow, not a chronological attack lifecycle. Validation and analyst judgment are required before operational action.

figures.title: Three statistical forms

panels.label: Point
panels.text: One observation differs from a stated comparison distribution.

panels.label: Contextual
panels.text: The same action differs in meaning across role, time or workload context.

panels.label: Collective
panels.text: Related observations form an unusual pattern when considered together.

figures.boundary: Forms can overlap. None establishes malicious intent.
figures.caption: Schematic examples of statistical forms. Dot positions and shapes are illustrations, not incident measurements.

figures.title: Rare events change alert precision
figures.boundary: These assumed counts explain base rates; they are not measured detector results.
figures.caption: Precision uses all alerts as its denominator; false-positive rate uses all benign events. A 1% false-positive rate does not mean 99% alert precision.

figures.title: How much moved?
figures.subtitle: Volumetric

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Count bytes, objects, rows or events; do not substitute one for another.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Compare like workloads over equal observation windows.

figures.boundary: Backups, reporting and recovery can produce legitimate spikes.
figures.caption: Volumetric: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: How often did it happen?
figures.subtitle: Frequency / Rate

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Count occurrences and state the time denominator.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Evaluate rate with source and target diversity.

figures.boundary: Retries, polling and releases can create bursts; sparse attacks may not.
figures.caption: Frequency / Rate: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Does the timing fit the task?
figures.subtitle: Temporal

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Preserve event time, time zone, shift and schedule.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Compare equivalent calendar periods, not just clock hours.

figures.boundary: On-call work, travel and daylight-saving changes can explain timing.
figures.caption: Temporal: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Compare the right peers
figures.subtitle: Peer-Group

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Define role and cohort membership before scoring.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Compare like entities; reassess after a legitimate role change.

figures.boundary: Small cohorts and incomplete inventory can manufacture an outlier.
figures.caption: Peer-Group: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Order adds context
figures.subtitle: Sequence

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Join a defined entity or session across ordered events.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Declare permitted gaps, missing steps and late arrival.

figures.boundary: This illustrative workflow can also be legitimate; timing alone is not causality.
figures.caption: Sequence: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: A new edge is a question
figures.subtitle: Graph / Relationship

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Define the direction and meaning of each edge.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Compare with a past-only relationship graph.

figures.boundary: Projects and migrations create legitimate edges; novelty is not attribution.
figures.caption: Graph / Relationship: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Network location is uncertain
figures.subtitle: Geographic / ASN

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Retain the source IP and enrichment version.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Correlate device, session and account history.

figures.boundary: IP geolocation is not a measurement of the person’s physical location.
figures.caption: Geographic / ASN: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Review identity and access changes
figures.subtitle: Identity / Access

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Collect factor lifecycle, consent and workload audit records.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Separate a recorded change from an inferred anomaly.

figures.boundary: Recovery and delegated administration can be authorized.
figures.caption: Identity / Access: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Rare does not mean malicious
figures.subtitle: Rare Process / Service

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Measure prevalence within a role and observation window.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Check signer, hash, owner and collection coverage.

figures.boundary: New software, diagnostics and newly enabled telemetry can all look rare.
figures.caption: Rare Process / Service: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Direct child is not any descendant
figures.subtitle: Parent-Child Execution

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Use stable process identifiers and parent identifiers.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Declare direct-child matching or an ancestry search.

figures.boundary: PID reuse, missing ancestry and in-process execution limit coverage.
figures.caption: Parent-Child Execution: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Track source, destination and units
figures.subtitle: Data Movement

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Keep audit events, unique objects, records and bytes distinct.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Review destination ownership and access authorization.

figures.boundary: Approved migration and backup can resemble exfiltration.
figures.caption: Data Movement: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Inspect usage, not just the port
figures.subtitle: Protocol / Application Usage

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Record parser version, sensor location and feature definition.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Compare the entity’s application and destination history.

figures.boundary: New clients and legitimate encoded identifiers can shift a baseline.
figures.caption: Protocol / Application Usage: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: No event is not the same as no activity
figures.subtitle: Negative Anomaly (Absence)

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Define when a source is expected to report.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Check delivery, asset state, filters and retention separately.

figures.boundary: An outage or parser failure can look like deliberate impairment.
figures.caption: Negative Anomaly (Absence): one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Compare before and after
figures.subtitle: State-Change

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Retain actor, object, timestamp and old/new values.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Check effective permissions and approved change records.

figures.boundary: A first-seen configuration change can be legitimate administration.
figures.caption: State-Change: one operational feature family, not a mutually exclusive statistical class. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Join evidence without inventing a chain
figures.subtitle: Multi-Event Correlation

panels.label: Measure
panels.text: Join tenant, account, host or session with bounded event time.

panels.label: Compare
panels.text: Retain missing or ambiguous links; deduplicate shared evidence.

figures.boundary: Adding a gate can remove true positives as well as false positives.
figures.caption: Multi-Event Correlation: a composition pattern, not an additional independent anomaly family. The incident cards below provide separate source-reported examples; this schematic does not reconstruct those incidents.

figures.title: Map behavior, then ask what is measurable

steps.label: Observed behavior
steps.text: Keep the source and its limits.

panels.label: ATT&CK v19.2 context
panels.text: The v19 split created Stealth and Defense Impairment. Tactics are not a required time sequence.

panels.label: Do not infer
panels.text: An anomaly tag is neither a technique verdict, a group identity nor measured detection coverage.

figures.boundary: These are analytical relationships, not a guaranteed attack progression.
figures.caption: The article’s tactic matrix is a set of proposed observation opportunities. It is not a ranking of detector performance.

figures.title: SUNBURST: observation is not an entropy score

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: A trojanized SolarWinds component used delayed activation and encoded information in DNS names.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Correlate DNS-label structure, destination novelty and the originating process.

figures.boundary: No measured victim entropy range or universal DNS cutoff is established here.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: Exchange: keep campaign evidence separate

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: Microsoft described Exchange exploitation and webshell deployment. Broader post-exploitation reporting includes multiple actors.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Join unusual web requests, ASPX writes and shell ancestry with the server’s role.

figures.boundary: Do not assign every post-exploitation observation to HAFNIUM. Standard IIS logs do not expose arbitrary request bodies.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: BazarCall to Conti: one intrusion account

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: The selected investigation describes BazarCall, Trickbot, Cobalt Strike and Conti in one intrusion.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Correlate enumeration, remote administration, share access and security changes by host and identity.

figures.boundary: This is not every affiliate’s timeline. Administrative tools and backup changes can be legitimate.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: OilRig-associated RDAT: variants matter

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: Unit 42 described RDAT communication mechanisms, including an email/steganography variant.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Inspect protocol structure, timing, destinations and endpoint context for the specific sample.

figures.boundary: Do not collapse every variant into DNS tunneling or treat a TXT:A ratio as a verdict.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: MOVEit: application account, not Windows user

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: LEMURLOOT interacted with the MOVEit database and created a MOVEit application account.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Correlate webshell access, application sessions, database changes and exports.

figures.boundary: Windows Security 4720 does not describe this SQL-backed application-account creation.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: Midnight Blizzard: preserve the actual permission

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: Microsoft reported password spraying, residential proxies and Exchange full_access_as_app permission abuse.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Join account failures, application consent and ownership, credentials and EWS activity.

figures.boundary: Do not substitute generic Graph mail scopes. Missing history is a cold start, not evidence of innocence.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: UNC3944: look across identity and SaaS

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: Mandiant described help-desk social engineering, identity abuse and SaaS data theft using legitimate integration tools.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Join factor changes to sessions and sensitive application actions with real tenant/account keys.

figures.boundary: A transfer can bypass endpoint sensors without leaving every provider or application blind.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: Storm-0558: customer-side detection did work

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: An acquired signing key was used to forge tokens. The CSRB describes State Department discovery using Big Yellow Taxi and MailItemsAccessed.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Use workload audit data and identity context; evaluate any proposed local analytic separately.

figures.boundary: The private rule and performance denominator are not published here. Storm-1283 OAuth cryptomining is a separate campaign.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: Volt Typhoon: the execution host matters

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: Microsoft described ntdsutil IFM credential extraction against domain controllers, with living-off-the-land activity.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Review IFM creation on the DC, its principal, approved backup context and subsequent data movement.

figures.boundary: A non-DC-only filter misses this execution context. A remote initiation host is not necessarily the execution host.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: APT41: two accounts, not one invented chain

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: 2019: MESSAGETAP was an ELF data miner on Linux SMS servers. 2024: SQLULDR2 exports and PINEGROVE transfers appear in a separate investigation.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Check process provenance and capture outputs for the first case; database exports and storage destinations for the second.

figures.boundary: Loading libpcap or using cloud storage is not proof of theft. These are separate reports, not sequential stages.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: Impacket is a toolkit, not an attribution

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: CISA AA22-277A reports Impacket and data theft without assigning a named actor.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Correlate remote logons, process ancestry and mode-specific evidence.

figures.boundary: secretsdump is not synonymous with DCSync. Ordinary wmiexec is not a permanent WMI subscription.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: 3CX: a signature is not a benign verdict

panels.label: Source-reported
panels.text: SentinelOne reported behavioral detections before public disclosure. GitHub-hosted icons carried encoded C2 information in the Windows chain.

panels.label: Detection hypothesis
panels.text: Investigate new destinations and later execution associated with a normally trusted application.

figures.boundary: The icons were not described as executable payloads. Vendor-reported detection is not an independent EDR benchmark.
figures.caption: The solid evidence panel summarizes cited reporting; the dashed hypothesis panel is author inference. No victim-telemetry replay or validation of the author’s proposed detector is implied.

figures.title: A field name is not a collection guarantee

panels.label: Distinct pipelines
panels.text: Security 4688 and Sysmon 1 are separate process-creation sources. Validate each adapter.

panels.label: Missing observations
panels.text: No event can mean no activity, disabled auditing, filtering, delay or failed collection.

figures.boundary: Validate raw records before treating a normalized table as detection coverage.
figures.caption: A telemetry contract connects source meaning to query assumptions. This diagram does not imply that a SIEM enables collection automatically.

figures.title: High entropy is not proof of tunneling

panels.label: Definition
panels.text: H = −Σ p(c) log₂ p(c), in bits per character. Count characters in the selected label.

panels.label: Bound
panels.text: For length n and alphabet A: H ≤ log₂(min(n, |A|)). Label selection and case normalization matter.

figures.boundary: abcd is structured, yet has 2 bits/character. This feature does not measure intent.
figures.caption: The values are computed from the displayed strings. The maintained query is an ASCII-label feature extractor; it is not a SUNBURST detector or a universal tunneling threshold.

figures.title: Kerberoasting: request evidence versus outcome

steps.label: Investigation
steps.text: Ticket requests do not prove offline recovery.

panels.label: Encryption scope
panels.text: RC4 is 0x17; AES types include 0x11 and 0x12. RC4-only filters miss AES activity.

panels.label: Known blind spot
panels.text: The public one-record replay produces no match for the service-breadth rule.

figures.boundary: No blanket exclusion for every account or service whose name ends in $.
figures.caption: The statistic is distinct-service breadth, not proof that a ticket was cracked. The displayed blind spot is retained from the existing replay report.

figures.title: DCSync: keep source correlation honest

steps.label: Bounded join
steps.text: Same DC + normalized logon ID + event time.

steps.label: 4624 context
steps.text: Use a suitable matching logon, if available.

panels.label: Prerequisite
panels.text: Directory Service Access auditing + applicable SACL. A SACL selects auditing; it does not grant rights.

panels.label: Unresolved is a valid result
panels.text: 4662 has no native client-IP field. Retain candidates when source enrichment is missing or ambiguous.

figures.boundary: One matching replication right does not prove successful credential extraction.
figures.caption: Arrows show an enrichment workflow, not the temporal order of the Windows events. Approved replication needs scoped inventory-backed context, not a name-based exemption.

figures.title: Pass-the-Hash: two hunting views, no single verdict

panels.label: Target-side view
panels.text: 4624 type 3 with NTLM can describe ordinary network authentication.

panels.label: Source-side view
panels.text: Type 9 NewCredentials with seclogo can appear in some implementations and legitimate alternate-credential workflows.

figures.boundary: The NTLM hash is not sent as the password. Context and implementation-specific evidence are required.
figures.caption: Neither view proves PtH, and not every implementation produces both. Correlate account, source process, destination and authorized administration.

figures.title: LSASS process access needs provenance

steps.label: Sysmon 10
steps.text: Source, target, time and access mask.

steps.label: Process context
steps.text: Signer, hash, ancestry and call trace.

steps.label: Investigation
steps.text: Compare authorized security and diagnostic tools.

panels.label: 0x1010
panels.text: VM read + limited query information.

panels.label: 0x1410
panels.text: The same rights plus query information.

figures.boundary: An access mask or unresolved call trace alone does not establish dumping or injection.
figures.caption: Bitmask meanings are separate from malicious intent. A familiar filename, signer or directory is not a universal safe exclusion.

figures.title: A detector can miss at different layers

steps.label: Data pipeline
steps.text: Drops, filters, clock or parser errors.

panels.label: Investigate the layer
panels.text: Record which assumption failed and test an alternative source or analytic.

panels.label: Avoid circular reasoning
panels.text: A missing alert does not prove intentional evasion or absence of compromise.

figures.boundary: This is a diagnostic map, not a sourced chronology for any particular actor.
figures.caption: Different failure layers require different remedies. More complex scoring cannot recover events the pipeline never collected.

figures.title: Make the analytic reproducible

steps.label: Define
steps.text: Entity, units, windows and missing-data behavior.

figures.boundary: Eight normalized KQL examples are not eight drop-in native Sentinel connectors.
figures.caption: Passing syntax and functional fixtures is one stage. Native ingestion, field compatibility and production value remain separate validation tasks.

figures.title: What the tests actually establish
figures.boundary: Query output rows are candidates, not labeled true positives. Production accuracy is not established.
figures.caption: Counts are read from the committed execution report, not rerun by drawing the figure. The zero-match Kerberoasting case remains visible.

figures.title: Close the loop before operational use

steps.label: Collect
steps.text: Generate and inspect real source events.

steps.label: Replay
steps.text: Include authorized benign and attack cases.

steps.label: Shadow
steps.text: Measure alerts, misses and analyst effort.

steps.label: Review
steps.text: Assign an owner, rollback and revalidation plan.

figures.boundary: Investigation priority, incident declaration and automatic containment are different decisions.
figures.caption: A proposed operational workflow. This article has not completed a representative production trial or certified automated containment safety.

figures.title: Freeze the experiment before the test
figures.boundary: The generator is a constructed world, not a representative enterprise sample.
figures.caption: Chronological train, validation and test partitions are disjoint. The gated-MAD model reuses the ungated threshold; the test is not used for tuning.

figures.title: Corroboration reduces alerts and recall
figures.boundary: The generator makes corroboration more likely for attacks. That advantage is assumed, not discovered.
figures.caption: Confusion counts and precision/recall are computed from the committed study. Compared with ungated entity-MAD, the gate removes both false and true alerts; it is not a free improvement.
